sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Production observability for Rails means more than log files. This page covers the three pillars — logs, metrics, traces — in the Rails context: Lograge replaces Rails' noisy multi-line request log with a single structured JSON line that includes controller, action, duration, and status; Semantic Logger adds correlation IDs and structured fields. rack-mini-profiler shows SQL queries and rendering time in development; Skylight, Scout, and Datadog APM provide distributed tracing in production. rbspy samples a running Ruby process without restart — the depth marker for production profiling. Sentry captures exceptions with stack traces, release tracking, and sampling. The SLO/SLI section covers the four golden signals and how to define error budgets for a Rails API. The incident response section covers the blameless post-mortem format.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: structured-logging, apm-profiling-ruby, error-tracking, slo-sli, incident-response. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
